mutations.find: if (r == null) throw new Error(`${label}: no spawn result to read — NO VERDICT`)
expectRed: a missing result is reported as no verdict, naming what ran
mutations.note: Without it a missing result dies on `r.error` with a bare TypeError, naming neither the caller nor the fact that nothing was graded.

expectRed: a timed-out run names the budget it exceeded, not a spawn failure
a timed-out run with no stated budget still reports a timeout
a real child that outruns its timeout is reported as no verdict
mutations.note: spawnSync sets BOTH `error` and `signal` on a timeout, so the generic branch reports 'could not spawn' for a child that spawned fine and then ran long. Encoded as a deletion rather than a reordering: removing the block is what makes the generic branch fire first, and it is the only anchor the find/replace schema can address.

mutations.find: if (r.signal) throw new Error(`${label}: killed by ${r.signal} — NO VERDICT`)
expectRed: a killed run is reported as no verdict, naming the signal
a real child killed by a signal is reported as no verdict
mutations.note: This IS #1303: the caller then sees status null and asserts on it. Both tests still throw via the status backstop below, so each is pinned by the MESSAGE, not by the presence of a throw.

mutations.find: throw new Error(`${label}: exited with no status and no signal — NO VERDICT`)
expectRed: a run with neither a status nor a signal is not treated as gradable
mutations.note: A result carrying no status, no signal and no error would pass as gradable and the caller would compare an exit code against null.

mutations.find: if (err.signal) throw new Error(`${label}: killed by ${err.signal} — NO VERDICT`)
expectRed: a thrown child killed by a signal is not converted into a verdict
mutations.note: The false-GREEN half of the class: `assert.notEqual(err.status, 0)` passes on null, so a killed child reads as a successful non-zero-exit assertion.

expectRed: a thrown child that never reached an exit code is not converted into a verdict
mutations.note: A spawn that never became a process would return `{status: undefined}` and read as an ordinary non-zero exit.

mutations.find:
if (r.status != null) return
  if (r.error) throw new Error(`${label}: could not spawn — ${r.error.message}`)
mutations.replace:
if (r.error) throw new Error(`${label}: could not spawn — ${r.error.message}`)
  if (r.status != null) return
expectRed: a run that answered is graded even though the input pipe broke
mutations.note: spawnSync sets EPIPE on the input write when the child stops reading stdin early and exits cleanly — a guard short-circuiting on an oversized payload does exactly that. Reading `error` before `status` reports that real verdict as a failed spawn, which is the defect this file exists to end, one level up. Found by a call site, not by review.

mutations.find: if (err == null) throw new Error(`${label}: no error to read — NO VERDICT`)
expectRed: a missing error object is reported as no verdict
mutations.note: The twin of drop-null-result-branch on the catch side: without it a missing error dies on `err.signal` with a bare TypeError, naming neither the caller nor the fact that nothing was graded.

mutations.find: if (r.error) throw new Error(`${label}: could not spawn — ${r.error.message}`)
expectRed: a child that never started names the underlying cause
mutations.note: ENOENT and EACCES then fall to the backstop and report 'no status and no signal', losing the cause the caller needs. status-outranks-error reorders this line but never removes it, so the line was reachable by no mutation.

mutations.find: return { status: err.status, stdout: String(err.stdout ?? ''), stderr: String(err.stderr ?? '') }
mutations.replace: return { status: err.status, stdout: err.stdout, stderr: err.stderr }
expectRed: a thrown child with no captured output yields empty strings, never undefined
mutations.note: Callers run `assert.match(stderr, /x/)`; an undefined stderr throws a TypeError naming neither the guard nor the expectation.

notEncoded.claim: runNode's `opts.timeout ?? 60_000` default — removing it restores an unbounded wait.
notEncoded.why: Grading it needs a test whose child never exits. With the default gone that test HANGS rather than going red, so the harness reports its own suite timeout as a fault instead of catching the mutation. A claim that can only be observed by hanging the grader is not encodable here.
